title: Finite constant-model witnesses under stratification conversion and isomorphism
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$, with restriction along scheme morphisms as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Use finite constant scalar models and the affine-local constructibility convention of [sk-def-sfb-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. A finite locally closed stratification consists of pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets $T_a$ covering $T$, together with immersions $s_a:S_a\to T$ having these images [def-constructible-stratification]. A constructible stratification has in addition a proof that every $T_a$ is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset].

For any predicate $P(S,s)$ on schemes over $T$, giving a constructible stratification with $P(S_a,s_a)$ for every $a$ is equivalent to giving a finite locally closed stratification, constructibility of its subsets separately, and those same assertions $P(S_a,s_a)$. The conversion retains the number, subsets, stratum schemes and immersion maps exactly.

If $e:M\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal A_T$, every finite constant-model witness for $M$ yields one for $N$ with the same pro-étale cover and the same finitely presented $\Lambda(*)$-modules. Every constructible-stratification witness for $M$ likewise yields one for $N$ with the same strata, covers and scalar modules; this also holds on every affine open in the non-qcqs convention.

Consequently, let $L\in D(\mathcal A_T)$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], let $M_q\in\mathcal A_T$ for each integer $q$, and suppose isomorphisms $e_q:M_q\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(L)$ are given. If each $M_q$ is constructible, then each $H^q(L)$ is constructible with the transported witnesses just specified. If moreover $M_q=0$ outside a finite interval $[r,s]$, then $L$ belongs to $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ with the same cohomological interval. No Tor-amplitude assertion is included.

proof.text: Unpack a constructible stratification as its finite index set, subsets $T_a$, schemes $S_a$, immersion maps $s_a$, partition and image proofs, and proofs $c_a$ of constructibility. Forget only the fields $c_a$, retaining them as a separate family. Conversely, adjoin the supplied $c_a$ to a finite locally closed stratification. These operations leave all data fields unchanged and return the same assertions $P(S_a,s_a)$, since their arguments have not changed. Repacking after unpacking recovers the original witness up to equality of proof fields. No reduced scheme structure or new immersion is chosen.

proof.text: For a model witness choose its cover $u_i:U_i\to T$, scalar modules $P_i$ and isomorphisms $\phi_i:u_i^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i$. Set $\psi_i=\phi_i\circ u_i^*(e^{-1})$. Its inverse is $u_i^*(e)\circ\phi_i^{-1}$: both composites are identities by functoriality of $u_i^*$ and the inverse identities for $e$ and $\phi_i$. Thus $\psi_i$ is the required model isomorphism for $N$. Retain the original cover, $P_i$ and finite-presentation proofs; neither their coefficients nor their presentations change.

proof.text: Given a constructible-stratification witness for $M$, retain its entire stratification, including constructibility proofs. For every $s_a:S_a\to T$, the two maps $s_a^*(e)$ and $s_a^*(e^{-1})$ are inverse, again by the functor laws. Apply step 2 on $S_a$ with this isomorphism and its existing model witness. This produces models for $s_a^*N$ on exactly the same covers and with exactly the same scalar modules. The defining existential quantifiers for constructibility are therefore satisfied by the original stratum data and these new isomorphisms.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: finite stratification witnesses and the passage from j_!H^q(K) to H^q(D(j_!)K); returned proof step 3, including its stratification adapter.

proof.text: In the affine-local convention, fix any affine open $v:V\hookrightarrow T$. Restrict $e$ and $e^{-1}$ along $v$; their composites are identities by functoriality. Apply step 3 to the given constructibility witness for $v^*M$. Its strata, covers and scalar modules now witness constructibility of $v^*N$. Since $V$ was arbitrary this proves the affine-local assertion. It makes no claim that witnesses on different affine opens form one finite stratification of a non-qcqs scheme.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: finite stratification witnesses and the passage from j_!H^q(K) to H^q(D(j_!)K); returned proof step 3, including its stratification adapter.

proof.text: For each integer $q$, apply steps 3 and 4 to $e_q:M_q\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(L)$ and a constructibility witness for $M_q$. This gives the stated witnesses for $H^q(L)$. If $q<r$ or $s<q$, compose $e_q^{-1}$ with $M_q\simeq0$ to obtain $H^q(L)\simeq0$. An object isomorphic to zero is zero: composing any map to or from it with the isomorphism reduces uniqueness to the zero object. Hence the cohomology vanishes outside the same interval $[r,s]$. Boundedness together with the constructible cohomology just proved is precisely membership in $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ in the finite constant-model convention; no tensor-product condition is used.
